_meta.indication: For the treatment of adult and pediatric patients 12 years and older with Grade 2 astrocytoma or oligodendroglioma with a susceptible IDH1 or IDH2 mutation following surgery including biopsy, sub-total resection, or gross total resection

pivotal_trials.population: Patients with Grade 2, IDH1 or IDH2 mutant astrocytoma or oligodendroglioma who had prior surgery including biopsy, sub-total resection, or gross total resection
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Radiographic PFS per blinded independent central review (BICR) according to RANO-LGG criteria; secondary endpoints included time to next intervention (TTNI), ORR, DOR, and OS
pivotal_trials.result: Median PFS 27.7 months (95% CI: 17, NE) vorasidenib vs 11.1 months (95% CI: 11, 13.7) placebo; HR 0.39 (95% CI: 0.27, 0.56; p<0.0001). Key secondary TTNI: not reached vs 17.8 months placebo; HR 0.26 (95% CI: 0.15, 0.43; p<0.0001).

key_safety: Serious adverse reactions occurred in 9% of patients. Most common (≥15%) adverse reactions were fatigue (33%), headache (28%), COVID-19 (28%), musculoskeletal pain (24%), diarrhea (21%), nausea (20%), seizure (16%), and dizziness (14%). Most common Grade 3/4 lab abnormalities were increased ALT (9%), increased AST (4.8%), increased GGT (2.2%), and decreased neutrophils (2.2%).
target_moa: Small molecule inhibitor targeting IDH1 and IDH2 enzymes; inhibits wild type and mutant variants (including IDH1 R132H) and decreases production of 2-hydroxyglutarate (2-HG) in IDH-mutant tumors

rems.type: No REMS required; no significant safety concerns warranting a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy were identified.

advisory_committee.vote: FDA did not refer this application to an advisory committee as no significant efficacy or safety issues were identified during the review.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan drug designation granted September 10, 2018 for the treatment of patients with glioma that harbors an IDH mutation

citations.quote: 10 September 2018	Orphan drug designation for the treatment of patients with glioma that harbors an IDH mutation was granted.

summary.text: VORANIGO received traditional (full) approval under a Priority Review NDA, based on the INDIGO trial; it had orphan drug designation for glioma with an IDH mutation.

citations.quote: The recommendation for traditional approval is based on the results from INDIGO (Study AG881-C-004, NCT04164901), which demonstrated that treatment with vorasidenib resulted in a statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvement in progression-free survival (PFS) compared to placebo in the indicated patient population.
